newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end off as mkt awaits Q1 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end off as mkt awaits Q1 earnings.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed down for the second straight day on Friday. Analysts and traders cited a continuation of light profit-taking begun Thursday after strong gains earlier in the week.

"We feel that stocks are assimilating prices after a brisk rebound at the beginning of the week. It was a cautious market awaiting new developments on the macroeconomic front and first quarter earnings reports," said Esteban Rojas, associate research director at the Arka brokerage in Mexico City.
The leading IPC share index .MXX ended down 9.94 points, or 0.26 percent, at 3,788.43.
Traders noted volume .TV.MX was restrained at million shares traded.
"Shares were mainly down in tandem with ADRs, which decoupled from the Dow Jones, but no way was it a sell-off," a floor trader said.
"Sales were settled at little volume and buyers stepped in every time we slid 10 points. Besides, they like to window-dress a little at the end of the week," he added.
"The tendency is often to slide when volume is thin," another floor trader added.
Traders said volume was also low due to lack of foreign investors in the market.
"Foreigners were present, but there were much less than on Wednesday," a floor trader said.
Dealers said profit-taking was most notable on blue chips such as telecomms firm Telmex, holding companies Grupo Carso and Femsa, and conglomerate Alfa.
Telmex shares ended down 10 centavos at 16.48 pesos, while its ADRs ended off 1/8 to 41-3/8. Grupo Carso A1 shares declined 60 centavos to 46.90 pesos, while Femsa fell 70 centavos to 38.90 pesos.
Alfa slid 85 centavos to 44.15 pesos.
Brokers noted three blue chips gained on favorable corporate news.
Media group Televisa, which stumbled on Thursday following news its long-serving chairman had died, recovered to end up 20 centavos at 102.80 pesos.

Press reports said new legislation approved on Thursday will allow Televisa to enter the digital television market in Spain. Approval was also reportedly given to merge Panamasat, in which Televisa has a minority share, with U.S. Hughes Communicatios Galaxy.

Glassmaker Vitro gained 50 centavos to 21.00 pesos in the wake of an announcement it was to sell its raw materials division for $131 million in cash. Vitro ADRs meanwhile performed better than many Mexican ADRs by gaining 1/4 to 8.
Mining company Penoles gained 30 centavos to 37.20 pesos on favorable reaction to news it had won a bidding process to buy the La Oroya smelting and refining complex in Peru.
Dealers also noted that heavily traded financial stock GFB B shares ended up four centavos at 2.76 pesos.

"GFB had been hit hard recently, and for those who bought at 2.50 pesos, the opportunity cost of selling it is still too high. They'll wait until it gains some more before selling," a floor trader said.
The broad market did not reflect performance by blue chips. A total of 108 stocks changed hands, of which gainers outnumbered sliders by 37 to 35.
(( --Martin Roberts, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7907))
